newsitem.title: UK: U. Utilities rejects windfall tax principle.
newsitem.headline: U. Utilities rejects windfall tax principle.

text.p: British multi-utility United Utilities plc said on Thursday it did not support the principle of a "windfall" tax as proposed by the government but if there were a levy, it should be a one-off charge raised just on its regulated business and "at a reasonable level."

United also said that pretax profits before exceptionals were up 14 percent to 444 million pounds ($726.5 million), but took an exceptional charge of 87 million and a loss on disposals of 77.1 million, with a total dividend payout of 37.2 pence per share, up from 32.7 pence.

United, which was formed when North West Water took over regional electricity company (Rec) Norweb at the start of 1996, said it had delivered promises made over the acquisition, "but the most significant achievement has been laying sound foundations for future growth."

The company added it intended to continue with principles to balance corporate and social responsibilities with equal attention to all stakeholders and said it strongly hoped such actions "will be recognised and offset from any eventual levy."
The new Labour government has vowed to introduce a one-off tax on the "excess profits" of privatised utilities but details will not be revealed until the government's forthcoming budget.
The government recently introduced a 10-point plan for improvements in services to cope with the country's worst drought for 200 years.

United Utilities said "excellent" progress had been made in integrating the electricity and water businesses and it was "confident that our goal of 474 million pounds of cumulative savings by March 2000 will be met". ($ = 0.611 British Pounds)
